questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $3\times2$ matrix with full singular value decomposition $A=U\Sigma V^{\top}$. What are the sizes of $U$, $\Sigma$ and $V$?
Which real matrices $A$ have a singular value decomposition $A=U\Sigma V^{\top}$ with $U$, $V$ orthogonal and $\Sigma$ diagonal with nonnegative entries?
options: Every real matrix, of any size or rank

questions.question: Let $A=U\Sigma V^{\top}$ be a singular value decomposition. Which factor acts first on $\boldsymbol{x}$ in the map $\boldsymbol{x}\mapsto A\boldsymbol{x}$, and what does it do?
options: $V^{\top}$, which rotates or reflects, taking $\boldsymbol{v}_i$ to $\boldsymbol{e}_i$
$U$, which turns the standard axes into the output directions $\boldsymbol{u}_i$
$\Sigma$, which stretches each coordinate axis by its $\sigma_i$
$V$, which carries the standard basis onto the vectors $\boldsymbol{v}_i$

questions.question: Which factorization is a singular value decomposition $U\Sigma V^{\top}$ of $A=\begin{pmatrix}-2&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$?

Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&2\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$, with $\sigma_1=\sqrt{10}$ and right singular vector $\boldsymbol{v}_1=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(1,1)^{\top}$. What is the left singular vector $\boldsymbol{u}_1$?
A real $2\times3$ matrix $A$ has singular values $\sigma_1=3$ and $\sigma_2=1$. What are the eigenvalues of the $3\times3$ matrix $A^{\top}A$?

A real $2\times2$ matrix has rank-one expansion $A=3\boldsymbol{u}_1\boldsymbol{v}_1^{\top}+1\cdot\boldsymbol{u}_2\boldsymbol{v}_2^{\top}$ with $\boldsymbol{u}_1=\boldsymbol{e}_1$, $\boldsymbol{v}_1=\boldsymbol{e}_2$, $\boldsymbol{u}_2=\boldsymbol{e}_2$, $\boldsymbol{v}_2=\boldsymbol{e}_1$. What is $A$?
A real $4\times3$ matrix $A$ has rank $2$. Which statement about its reduced SVD $A=U_r\Sigma_rV_r^{\top}$ is correct?
options: $U_r$ is $4\times4$ and $V_r$ is $3\times3$, as in the full SVD
It exists only for full rank $r=\min(m,n)=3$, which this matrix lacks

questions.question: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\2&0\\2&0\end{pmatrix}$, a $3\times2$ matrix of rank one. Which triple gives $\sigma_1$, $\boldsymbol{u}_1\in\mathbb{R}^3$ and $\boldsymbol{v}_1\in\mathbb{R}^2$ with $A=\sigma_1\boldsymbol{u}_1\boldsymbol{v}_1^{\top}$?

$A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$ has SVD with $\sigma_1=2$, $\sigma_2=0$, $\boldsymbol{u}_1=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(1,1,0)^{\top}$, $\boldsymbol{u}_2=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(1,-1,0)^{\top}$, $\boldsymbol{u}_3=(0,0,1)^{\top}$, $\boldsymbol{v}_2=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(1,-1)^{\top}$. Which vectors are an orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{Null}(A^{\top})$?

Let $A=U\Sigma V^{\top}$ be a full SVD of a real $m\times n$ matrix, with columns $\boldsymbol{u}_i$ of $U$, $\boldsymbol{v}_i$ of $V$ and singular values $\sigma_i$. Which relation is guaranteed for every such $A$ and each $1\le i\le p=\min(m,n)$?

Let $A=U\Sigma V^{\top}$ be an SVD of a real $2\times2$ matrix with $\sigma_1>\sigma_2>0$ and columns $\boldsymbol{u}_1,\boldsymbol{u}_2$ and $\boldsymbol{v}_1,\boldsymbol{v}_2$. Which change always gives another SVD of $A$ under these assumptions?
options: Negate only $\boldsymbol{u}_1$, keeping $\boldsymbol{v}_1$ as it is
Swap the roles of $U$ and $V$ in the product

questions.question: Let $A=U\Sigma V^{\top}$ be a full SVD of a real $m\times n$ matrix. Which matrix is guaranteed to have the columns $\boldsymbol{v}_i$ of $V$ as orthonormal eigenvectors with the listed eigenvalues, for every such $A$?

Let $A=U\Sigma V^{\top}$ be a singular value decomposition of a real invertible $2\times2$ matrix, with $\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(4,2)$, columns $\boldsymbol{u}_1,\boldsymbol{u}_2$ of $U$ and $\boldsymbol{v}_1,\boldsymbol{v}_2$ of $V$. Which expression for $A^{-1}\boldsymbol{u}_1$ is guaranteed without assuming $U=V$?
Let $Q$ be a $2\times2$ orthogonal matrix and $A=2Q$. Which statement about the singular value decompositions $A=U\Sigma V^{\top}$ is guaranteed for every real orthogonal $Q$?
options: The SVD is unique, as the singular values are fixed

questions.question: In the constructive proof of the SVD for a real $m\times n$ matrix of rank $r<m$, the vectors $\boldsymbol{u}_i=A\boldsymbol{v}_i/\sigma_i$ are used only for $i\le r$. Which construction of the remaining columns of $U$ is valid for every such $A$?
options: By the same formula, since $A\boldsymbol{v}_i/\sigma_i$ works for all $i$
As further eigenvectors of $A^{\top}A$, which lie in $\mathbb{R}^m$
By completing $\boldsymbol{u}_1,\ldots,\boldsymbol{u}_r$ to an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{R}^m$
They are left zero, since $\sigma_i=0$ for $i>r$

questions.question: The matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&-2\\3&0\end{pmatrix}$ maps the unit circle $\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon\|\boldsymbol{x}\|=1\}$ onto an ellipse. Using its singular value decomposition, what are the semi-axes of this ellipse?
options: Length $3$ along the $x$-axis and length $2$ along the $y$-axis
Length $3$ along the $y$-axis and length $2$ along the $x$-axis
Length $9$ along the $y$-axis and length $4$ along the $x$-axis
A circle of radius $\sqrt{6}$: all semi-axes have length $\sqrt{6}$
